r.description: Circular walk. Dog Friendly, Paths can be slippery in winter, Box Hill, Broadwood's tower folly, Juniper Valley, Happy Valley, Salomons Memorial Viewpoint

r.name: Box Hill Juniper Top circular walk, Box Hill
r.description: Paths can be slippery in winter, Dog friendly, viewpoints, Juniper bottom, Bluebells, Three grand houses, Happy Valley, Natural Play Trail

r.name: Box Hill Train To Stepping Stones Walk, Box Hill
Box Hill Stepping Stones walk, Box Hill
The Box Hill Hike, Box Hill
r.description: Circular walk, dog friendly, steep climbs and steps, paths may be slippery in winter, Please take care with your footing and wear suitable footwear for the conditions, Broadwood's Folly, Mickleham Gallops

r.name: Headley Heath Bluebell Walk, Box Hill
r.description: Discover distant vistas, wander through woodlands & valleys and enjoy a vast display of bluebells in the spring months on this family-friendly trail. Paths with some steep ascents and descents, steps, uneven terrain & bridlepaths. Dogs welcome on a lead.

r.name: Headley Heath Butterfly Walk, Box Hill
r.description: 2-mile circular walk round Headley Heath, rambling through woodland & heathland. Many different species of butterfly. Mainly flat or gently undulating land, with a some slight descents and ascents. Can be muddy. Dogs welcome under close control.

r.name: Headley Heath Circuit, Box Hill
r.description: Enjoy stunning views and rich, varied and rare wildlife on a circular walk over open heathland, woodland and chalk downland designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest. One steep descent and some steps. Dogs welcome on a lead due to livestock.

r.name: Headley Heath Lizard Trail, Box Hill
r.description: The Lizard Trail is a wonderful way to explore the rich array of flowers, birds, insects and animals that inhabit Headley Heath's rare environment of acid lowland heath and dry chalk downland. Dogs welcome, under control around livestock.

r.name: Headley Heath to White Hill Walking Trail, Box Hill
r.description: Take in views of the Surrey Hills on this circular walk through woodland, open pasture & farmland. There's a country pub to stop off at en route, and two steep slopes (between ponds and along a rocky bridlepath). Please keep dogs on leads near livestock.

r.name: Headley Heath Second World War Walking Trail, Box Hill
r.description: Learn Headley Heaths military past; In the 1940s it was devoid of shrubs & oak & was pockmarked with trenches, bomb craters & fox holes. Secrets & espionage were daily at Bellasis House. Challenging walk: steep climbs & descents. Dogs on leads near cattle

r.name: Headley Heath Military Trail, Box Hill
Osterley Trail, Osterley
r.description: Meander through Osterley's estate on this circular, taking in original vistas of the House across Middle Lake. Enjoy R. Adam's landscape along the carriageway, with open fields of livestock, woodland areas & tree lined avenues. Suitable for all abilities.

r.name: Polesden Lacey Ranger Run, Polesden Lacey
r.description: A scenic trail run along the waymarked Trust 10 route, taking in Grade II registered parkland & 400 year old SSSI woodland. Find countryside views & nearby Box Hill, Leith Hill & the North Downs Way: all great for on-foot exploration. Steep slopes.

r.name: Polesden Lacey Butterfly Walk, Polesden Lacey
r.description: The Polesden Lacey estate is home to a large variety of butterflies. Ranmore Common, is a SSSI, which protects the wide variety of rare woodland birds, bats & butterflies found here. Potential livestock - please keep dogs under close control / on a lead

r.name: The long walk at Hatchlands Park, Hatchlands Park
r.description: Hatchlands is one of the largest country estates in the green belt around Greater London. Follow the boundary through woodland & parkland with distant views of the house & Surrey countryside. Follow pink waymarker arrows. Rough paths. Tramper available.

r.name: The Wix Wood at Hatchlands Park, Hatchlands Park
r.description: Hatchlands is one of the largest country estates in London's green belt. Cut across the centre of the estate through wood & parkland, past the childrens play area, with views of the house. Follow purple waymarker arrows. Rough paths. Tramper available.

r.name: New Haw Lock to Pyrford Lock Walk, River Wey Navigations
r.description: The River Wey Navigation linked the Thames and a large part of central southern England via the Basingstoke and the Wey and Arun canals. This walk covers parts of the Wey Navigation and the Basingstoke Canal.

r.name: Weybridge to New Haw Lock Walk, River Wey Navigations
r.description: This walk follows the route of the last commercial barges on the Wey Navigations. The large Wey barges, owned by Stevens and Sons, transported grain from the Royal Docks in London to Coxes Mill in Addlestone until the late 1960s.

r.name: Historic views of Ham House walk, Ham House
r.description: This three-mile circular walk takes in the historic views from Ham House into Richmond Park and at the top of Richmond Hill. It's the perfect walk to take when you've finished your visit at Ham House.

r.name: Richmond Station to Ham House Historic Scenic Walk, Ham House
r.description: Why not leave your car at home and follow this trail from Richmond Station? From urban bustle to some of the most beautiful urban greens in England, to the iconic view of the Thames from Richmond Hill.

r.name: Surrey Cycleway
r.description: Cycle route consisting of main loop plus link routes

r.name: Bookham Common Butterfly Walk, North Downs West
r.description: Walk through one of the best woods in England for sighting the elusive purple emperor butterfly, Britain's second largest butterfly, with a wingspan of over 8cm. It was first recorded here in June 2017, and now thrives here thanks to decades of work.

r.name: Bookham Common Activity Trail, North Downs West
r.description: Bookham Commons is a widely varied landscape, ranging from shady woodlands, to open grassland plains, to marshy ponds and wetlands. This provides a wonderful set of habitats for lots of wildlife. See how much you can spot as you wander along the paths.

r.name: Kingston Station to Ham House Walk, Ham House
r.description: Enjoy a gentle walk from Kingston Station to Ham House and Garden on this 4.5-mile long stroll along the river, learning some interesting historical facts along the way.

r.name: Waymarked Walk at Ranmore Common, North Downs West
